# Garden share: decomposition into functional plan stubs

**Status:** The decomposition is complete. The stubs are **not created yet**: the deterministic library
creates stubs, and the session runs it (see "Recommended session operations"). After the stubs exist,
the work **waits for the owner's OK** at the decomposition checkpoint. No Product Owner handoff, status
write or vision move happens before that OK.

## Ancestry read

- `plans/vision/garden-share.md`: read in full. Its status is `ready`.
- Canvas: there is none. Glob `plans/**/*` from the project root matched 1 file (the vision), so this
  decomposition uses the vision only.

## Readiness gate (my reading; the session still has to produce the deterministic verdict)

| Check | Kind | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| Problem statement | blocking | Present and specific: garden owners have unused space while people on the waiting list wait three years for a plot. The only matching is word of mouth. |

| Success criteria | blocking | Present: 3 criteria, all measurable (offer in under 5 min; find and request within 1 km in under 5 min; 50 plots shared in 6 months) |

## Story maps (backbone → stories)

The story IDs inside this file are internal markers for the dependency graph.

`[MVP]` marks a story on the **walking skeleton**: the thinnest end-to-end path through every

### Stub 1: Offer a garden plot (`garden-share-offer-a-garden-plot.md`)

**Goal:** Garden owners publish their unused space with its size and access times.
- **Actor:** Garden owner in the town who has garden space they do not use
- **Impact:** Publishes a plot on the service instead of relying on word of mouth. The public plot link is useful on its own: the owner can share it through word of mouth, which is the channel that exists today.
- **Success metric:** Median offer time (form opened → plot published) is under 5 minutes. The operator progress page (stub 3) measures it.

**Backbone:** 1. Offer a plot → 2. Keep the offer current

#### Activity 1.1: Offer a plot

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S1.1.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to offer a plot by entering its address, its size in m², its weekly access times and my email, and then confirming with a one-time link, so that my unused space is published where growers can find it.
  - Acceptance:
    - Required fields: address; size (whole m², 1–1000); at least one access slot (day plus from/to time); email. One optional free-text access note is allowed.
    - Example: "Kerkstraat 12", 20 m², Saturday 09:00–12:00, `owner@example.org` → submit → an email with a one-time link arrives. Clicking the link within 30 minutes publishes the plot with status `Available`.
    - On publish, the owner is shown and emailed (a) the public plot page link and (b) a private manage link.
    - The public plot page shows size, access times and the area or neighbourhood name. **It never shows the exact address.** The address is geocoded once. The exact point is stored privately, and the public point is the exact point snapped to a 100 m grid (see decisions).
    - A missing size or a missing access slot shows an inline error, and no email is sent.
    - An expired or reused link shows "This link has expired — send a new one", and the plot stays unpublished.
    - The timestamps "form opened" and "published" are recorded for the offer-time metric.
  - Depends on: none · Size: ~3 pts (about 3 days) · INVEST: I ✓ N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ⚠ (at the 3-day limit; see decisions) T ✓

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **S1.1.2** As a garden owner, I want to be told straight away when my address cannot be placed in the town, so that I do not publish a plot that no grower can find.
  - Acceptance: an address the geocoder cannot resolve, or one outside the configured town boundary, shows "We couldn't place this address in <town>. Check the street and number." before submit. Nothing is published, and a corrected valid address goes through the normal flow.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S1.1.3** As a garden owner, I want to add an optional description and one photo of the plot, so that growers can judge the sun, soil and water before they ask.
  - Acceptance: a description of up to 1000 characters and a JPEG/PNG photo of up to 5 MB both appear on the public plot page. EXIF location data is stripped from the photo before storage. A plot without a description or photo publishes unchanged.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

#### Activity 1.2: Keep the offer current

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S1.2.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to withdraw my plot from the manage link, so that I stop being asked for space I no longer have.
  - Acceptance: Withdraw → status `Withdrawn`. The public page shows "This plot is no longer offered" and has no request option. The plot is excluded from every query for `Available` plots. Pending requests on a withdrawn plot are handled by S3.1.3.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **S1.2.2** As a garden owner, I want to edit the size, access times and description of my plot, so that growers see what is true now.
  - Acceptance: changing Saturday 09:00–12:00 to Sunday 10:00–13:00 makes the public page show Sunday 10:00–13:00 on its next load. Edits use the same validation as publishing.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~1–2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S1.2.3** As a garden owner, I want to pause my plot and resume it later, so that I can stop requests for a season without re-entering everything.
  - Acceptance: Pause → status `Paused`. The page shows "Not taking requests right now", and the plot is excluded from `Available` queries. Resume → status `Available`, with every detail unchanged.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S1.2.4** As a returning garden owner, I want to sign in with my email and see all my plots with their status, so that I can manage them without the original email.
  - Acceptance: an owner with 2 plots (`Available`, `Paused`) enters their email and receives a one-time link. "My plots" then lists both plots with their status and the actions Edit, Pause/Resume and Withdraw. An unknown email gets the same "check your inbox" message, so the form does not reveal which emails have accounts.

### Stub 2: Find and request a nearby plot (`garden-share-find-and-request-a-nearby-plot.md`)

**Goal:** People on the waiting list find a plot within 1 km and ask for it.
- **Actor:** Person on the town's allotment waiting list who wants to grow vegetables
- **Impact:** Finds plots within 1 km and asks for one instead of waiting three years
- **Success metric:** Median request time (search started → request confirmed) for a plot within 1 km is under 5 minutes. The operator progress page (stub 3) measures it.

**Backbone:** 1. Find plots near me → 2. Request a plot

#### Activity 2.1: Find plots near me

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S2.1.1 [MVP]** As a grower on the waiting list, I want to enter my address or postcode and see the available plots within 1 km, nearest first, so that I can see at once which plots I could reach.
  - Acceptance:
    - Plots whose public points lie 0.4 km, 0.9 km and 1.3 km in a straight line from the entered postcode → the list shows the 0.4 km plot, then the 0.9 km plot, and does not show the 1.3 km plot.
    - Each row shows the distance (rounded to 0.1 km), the size in m², the access times and a link to the public plot page.
    - Only `Available` plots appear. Searching needs no sign-in.
    - An address outside the town shows the same message as S1.1.2.
    - The timestamp "search started" is recorded for the request-time metric.
  - Depends on: S1.1.1 · Size: ~2–3 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **S2.1.2** As a grower, I want to see the results on a map, so that I can judge which plots lie on my usual routes.
  - Acceptance: each result is a marker at its public (snapped) point, never at the exact address. Clicking a marker highlights its row in the list, and the reverse also works.
  - Depends on: S2.1.1 · Size: ~2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S2.1.3** As a grower, I want to filter the results by minimum size and by the days I am free, so that I only see plots I can actually use.
  - Acceptance: with three plots (10 m² on Saturday, 20 m² on Sunday, 25 m² on Saturday), the filter "≥ 15 m², Saturday" shows only the 25 m² Saturday plot. Clearing the filters shows all three.
  - Depends on: S2.1.1 · Size: ~1–2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S2.1.4** As a grower, I want a clear answer when no plot is within 1 km, so that I do not hit a dead end.
  - Acceptance: with no plot within 1 km and the nearest at 1.6 km, the page shows "No plots within 1 km right now. The nearest is 1.6 km away." with a link to it and options to widen the search to 2 km or 3 km. With no plots in the town at all, it says so.
  - Depends on: S2.1.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

#### Activity 2.2: Request a plot

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S2.2.1 [MVP]** As a grower, I want to request a plot from its page with a short message and confirm with my email, so that the owner knows who I am and why I want the plot.
  - Acceptance:
    - On an `Available` plot's page, the request form asks for: first name, email, a message of up to 500 characters, and a required checkbox "I am on <town>'s allotment waiting list". The grower then confirms with a one-time link.

- [ ] **S2.2.2** As a grower, I want to see my requests and their status, so that I know where I stand without emailing anyone.

  - Depends on: S2.2.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.2.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

### Stub 3: Answer requests and track sharing (`garden-share-answer-requests-and-track-sharing.md`)

**Goal:** Requests become shared plots, and the operator can see whether the vision's targets are being met.
- **Actors:** The garden owner answers requests. The service operator tracks the targets.
- **Impact:** The owner says yes or no to each request. Accepting connects owner and grower. The operator sees progress against all three success criteria.
- **Success metric:** 50 plots shared within six months of launch.

**Backbone:** 1. Answer a request → 2. Track sharing progress

#### Activity 3.1: Answer a request

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S3.1.1 [MVP]** As a garden owner, I want to accept a request from the request email or from my manage page, so that the grower can start using my plot.
  - Acceptance:
    - Accept → the request becomes `Accepted`, and the plot becomes `Shared`. A `Shared` plot is excluded from search and shows no request option.
    - Within 1 minute, the grower receives an email with the exact address, the access times and the owner's email. The owner receives an email with the grower's first name and email.
    - Every other `Pending` request for the plot becomes `Closed`. Each of those growers receives an email: "This plot has been shared with someone else", with a link to search again.
    - The accept link works once. Accepting a request that has already been withdrawn shows "This request was withdrawn".
  - Depends on: S2.2.1 · Size: ~3 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.2.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **S3.1.2** As a garden owner, I want to decline a request, with an optional short reply, so that the grower knows to look elsewhere and, if I choose, why.
  - Acceptance: Decline → the request becomes `Declined`, and the plot stays `Available`. The grower receives an email with the owner's reply (up to 300 characters, if given) and a link to search again from the grower's address.
  - Depends on: S2.2.1 · Size: ~1–2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.2.1; independent of S3.1.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓
- [ ] **S3.1.3** As a garden owner, I want my pending requests to be closed when I withdraw my plot, so that growers are not left waiting for a plot that is gone.
  - Acceptance: withdrawing a plot with 2 `Pending` requests → both become `Closed`, and each grower receives a "This plot is no longer offered" email. Pausing a plot keeps its `Pending` requests open (the owner can still answer them) and blocks new ones.
  - Depends on: S1.2.1, S2.2.1 · Size: ~1 pt · INVEST: I ✓ (after S1.2.1 and S2.2.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

#### Activity 3.2: Track sharing progress

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] **S3.2.1 [MVP]** As the service operator, I want a progress page showing the plots shared since launch against the target of 50 and the days left in the six-month window, so that I can see whether the vision is on track.
  - Acceptance:
    - Example: launch date 2027-03-01 is configured, 3 distinct plots have an `Accepted` request, and today is 2027-04-01 → the page shows "3 of 50 plots shared · 153 days left". It also shows the number of plots offered and requests sent.
    - A plot counts once.
    - Only emails on the configured operator allowlist can sign in.
    - The page reads the stored request and plot statuses, so it can be tested with seeded `Accepted` records.
  - Depends on: S2.2.1 · Size: ~2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.2.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **S3.2.2** As the service operator, I want the median offer time and the median request time, and the share of each that took under 5 minutes, so that I can check both five-minute criteria.
  - Acceptance:
    - Example: offers that took 3, 4 and 7 minutes → median 4:00, and 67% took under 5 minutes. Requests are reported the same way.
    - Both are shown for two windows: since launch, and the last 30 days.
    - Offer time runs from form opened to published (S1.1.1). Request time runs from search started to request confirmed (S2.1.1 → S2.2.1).
    - Requests with no search earlier in the same browser session (the grower arrived by a shared plot link) are counted separately as "direct link" and are not included in the median.
  - Depends on: S2.1.1, S2.2.1 · Size: ~2 pts · INVEST: I ✓ (after S2.1.1 and S2.2.1) N ✓ V ✓ E ✓ S ✓ T ✓

**Dependency order (stub 3):** 1. S3.1.1, S3.1.2, S3.2.1 (depend on S2.2.1 only); S3.1.3 (depends on S1.2.1 and S2.2.1); S3.2.2 (depends on S2.1.1 and S2.2.1). There are no dependencies inside stub 3.

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity

1. **Decomposed instead of handed back as a single plan.** The vision has 3 success criteria, two
   actors and three distinct impacts, so it needs more than one plan.
2. **Goals follow the journey (offer → find and request → answer), not the actors.** A split by actor
   (an owner stub and a grower stub) creates a cycle: the owner's accept or decline needs the grower's
   requests, and the grower's search needs the owner's plots. Merging everything into one stub gives 20
   stories, above the ceiling of 15 per stub. A merge of stubs 2 and 3 (13 stories, three actors) is
   possible with `mergeStubs` if the owner prefers fewer stubs.
3. **One stub per goal, with the walking skeleton marked in every stub.** This structure does not fix
   a build order. A thin path through all three stubs first and a stub-by-stub build are both possible.
   The owner chooses.
4. **No release phases.** The method's grouping of stories into release phases was replaced by the
   technical dependency graph plus the walking-skeleton marker. `[MVP]` means the story is on the
   thinnest end-to-end path. It is not a priority.
5. **Identity is an email address plus a one-time sign-in link, with no passwords.** Both owners and
   growers must be reachable by email, and a password form costs time inside the five-minute windows.
   The alternative is passwords or social login.
6. **The email is confirmed before a plot is published or a request is sent.** This keeps fake plots
   and fake requests out, but the email round trip counts inside both five-minute windows: slow email
   delivery puts criteria 1 and 2 at risk. The alternative is to publish at once and unpublish if the
   email is not confirmed within 24 hours. This is listed as an open question.
7. **The interface is a responsive website.** The vision excludes a mobile app.
8. **Location and distance.** The address is geocoded once. The exact point is stored privately, and
   a public point is stored as the exact point snapped to a 100 m grid. Search filtering, the distances
   shown and the map all use the public point, measured as straight-line distance. Filtering on the
   exact point would let anyone locate a house by moving the search point until a plot appears or
   disappears at the 1 km edge. The cost is that a distance can be off by up to about 71 m (half the
   diagonal of a 100 m cell). The alternative is walking distance from a routing service.
9. **The town is a configuration value.** The vision does not name the town, so the town's name,
   boundary polygon and launch date are settings.
10. **Waiting-list membership is self-declared** with a required checkbox. There is no check against
    the municipal list.
11. **A plot goes to one grower.** Accepting a request closes every other pending request for that
    plot, and each of those growers is told.
12. **"Shared" means a plot with an accepted request.** Each plot counts once. The six-month window
    starts at the configured launch date.
13. **A service operator actor was added**, with access through an email allowlist. The vision names
    no one who measures its success criteria, and without such a person the criteria cannot be checked.
14. **How the two times are measured.** Offer time runs from form opened to published. Request time
    runs from search started to request confirmed. Requests that arrive by a shared plot link without a
    search are counted separately and kept out of the median.
15. **Contact details are exchanged only on acceptance.** Before that, the owner sees only the grower's
    first name and message, and the grower sees only the area and the snapped distance.
16. **Field rules.**
    - Access times are weekly slots (day plus from/to time), with an optional note.
    - Size is a whole number of m², from 1 to 1000.
    - A request message is at most 500 characters, and a decline reply at most 300.
    - A photo is at most 5 MB, and its EXIF location data is stripped.
17. **Stories were shaped to keep every dependency chain at 3 stories or fewer.**
    - Publishing (S1.1.1) includes the email confirmation and the public plot page. This puts S1.1.1
      at the 3-day limit, which is flagged.
    - Requests are made from the plot page, so the request story does not depend on search.
    - Accepting and declining are separate stories.
    - Closing the other requests is part of accepting.
